specification.title: A migration whose reversal deletes its marker
steps: Runner A applies { m1 }. m1 inserts marker m1.
Revert with the framework's default selection. m1's reversal deletes marker m1.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the revert has returned and the reapply has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: If a revert reports a migration as reverted, its history entry is absent and its marker is absent.

execution.description: Django's documented default: transaction.atomic() for the outer transaction and a nested transaction.atomic() for the savepoint, PostgreSQL backend, psycopg 3, CONN_MAX_AGE 0, no connection pool. TX-03 is not run in this mode. The default closes the database connection at the end of each request (not-applicable-by-design for handing a transactionally active connection to later work). https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.1/ref/databases/#persistent-connections
execution.form: MigrationExecutor.migrate on a generated ppcs_mg.0001_m1 RunPython migration. forwards inserts the marker and, when the case holds the gate, waits on pg_advisory_xact_lock in that transaction.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: A reported revert says the migration's effects are gone. The next apply is what shows that history and the database agree: the migration runs again.

api_outcome.contract: Django 6.1 MigrationExecutor.migrate applies or unapplies the plan. On PostgreSQL the migration runs inside schema_editor(atomic=True) (django/db/migrations/executor.py). record_applied runs in that transaction when the migration has no deferred SQL. record_unapplied runs after the backwards transaction commits. The executor takes no advisory lock. RunPython without a reverse callable raises NotImplementedError from database_backwards and does not record the migration as unapplied.
